title: Sources, formats, captions, and accessibility
learningObjectives: Use sources, formats, captions, and accessibility accessibly and safely.

understand.concept: Browsers support media formats differently. source offers alternative files; track with kind="captions" provides synchronized text. Provide transcripts where appropriate.
understand.whyItMatters: Captions and transcripts make audio information available to more people and situations.
understand.analogy: Alternative sources are like alternate editions; they do not guarantee every format works.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy explains the idea only; browser behaviour depends on semantics, resource availability and format support.

explain.narrative: Browsers support media formats differently. source offers alternative files; track with kind="captions" provides synchronized text. Provide transcripts where appropriate.

examples.code: <video controls><source src="lesson.mp4" type="video/mp4"><track kind="captions" src="lesson-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default></video>
examples.explanation: Inspect each attribute and test with a media file you own or are permitted to use.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser renders the element when its resource exists and the format is supported.

practise.guidedTask: Add a captions track and describe what a WebVTT file contains.
practise.independentTask: Build an accessible media section for a fictional learning page and explain your choices.
hints: Check the browser console and network panel if a resource fails.
Do not embed untrusted content without reviewing its origin and permissions.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Sources, formats, captions, and accessibility</title></head><body>
<video controls><source src="lesson.mp4" type="video/mp4"><track kind="captions" src="lesson-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default></video>
</body></html>

questions.explanation: Choose the semantic element or attribute designed for this purpose.

questions.prompt: Does every image need long descriptive alt text?
questions.explanation: Alt depends on purpose; decorative images use an empty alt attribute.
